Filter swap logged 02:40. Fourth this month; the duty cycle says two. I ran the carbon budget twice and got the same answer both times, which is the problem.

Told control. That was eleven weeks ago. The ack came back in nine minutes and nothing since. The queue shows my message delivered, so it is not a comms fault.

I am not writing down what I think it means. If the next rotation asks me anything, I would tell them: watch the filter count.

TRAFFIC TAKES WEEKS. The terminal queues outbound messages and files replies when they arrive. A reply may never come. Plan as if it will not.

SENDING. Select a draft on the left to transmit it. Status reports are routine and usually answered. Questions are not.

READING. Unread traffic is marked with an asterisk. Highlight a message to read it.

Do not wait on the radio. The ship does not.

CO2 (ppm)
   5000   headache; reading numbers takes longer.
  15000   judgement slips; check your work twice.
  25000   breathing damage begins. Leave or fix it.

O2
  below 16 percent: slow thinking, then unconsciousness.
  below 10 percent: minutes.

COLD
  below 10 C: clumsy hands.
  below  3 C: exposure damage.

RATIONS
  the galley draws one ration per crew per day.
  at zero stock you starve; water runs out first.

If you feel fine, you are probably not. Read the panel.

The module loses heat to the exterior, which runs near -60 C. The heater runs on LIFE SUPPORT and holds the cabin near 21 C.

If the heater loses power the cabin cools fast. Below 10 C you lose dexterity. Below 3 C exposure becomes dangerous. Pipes freeze near 1 C.

If you return to a cold module: restore life support first, then wait. The heater is not fast. Dress the wound before you clean the tools.
